```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.5,
                      dpi = 120, comment = "#>")
```

This demo walks from the raw 2025 Demeritt Forest cruise to 50-year growth
projections. You'll use two growth engines and compare them. Run it
chunk by chunk in RStudio; every chunk is meant to be read, changed, and
re-run.

**What you need**

* R (≥ 4.1) and RStudio.
* The 2025 inventory folder (`2025_DBD_Inventory`). Set `data_dir` below if
  your copy lives somewhere else.
* *Optional:* the USDA Forest Service FVS executables
  (<https://www.fs.usda.gov/fvs/software/>). Section 7 needs them; everything
  else runs without FVS.

# Setup

Install once:

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
install.packages(c("remotes", "readxl", "ggplot2", "dplyr", "tidyr", "RSQLite", "DBI"))
remotes::install_github("piketremor/MEForLab")
```

Then, every session:

```{r libs}
library(MEForLab)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

data_dir <- params$data_dir
options(MEForLab.fvs_dir = params$fvs_dir)      # where FVSne(.exe) lives, if installed

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
          theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
                legend.position = "top"))
pal <- c("#2a78d6", "#eb6834", "#1baf7a", "#eda100")   # fixed series order
```

All package documentation is in R's help system. Try `?conus_project` or
`help(package = "MEForLab")`.

# From cruise to tree list

The overstory cruise is a BAF 20 prism sample of live trees ≥ 4.6 in. DBH. A
5.3-ft radius sapling plot is nested on each point (field instructions:
`INV_Project_66 field Instructions.docx`). Species use TallTimber numeric
codes, and crown ratio (in percent) was recorded in the `Tree_Notes` field.
Heights were *not* measured.

`read_demeritt_inventory()` does four things:

1. Expands each prism tree to trees per acre: TPA = BAF / (0.005454 · DBH²) / number of points in the stand.
2. Expands sapling counts by the fixed-plot factor (43,560 / π·5.3² ≈ 494 TPA per stem).
3. Translates species codes to FVS alpha and FIA codes.
4. Fills missing heights with the FVS-NE Wykoff equations (`wykoff.ht()`) and
   fills the few missing crown ratios.

```{r read}
trees <- read_demeritt_inventory(
  overstory = file.path(data_dir, "DBD_66_Tree_DataBAF20_StandsOK.xlsx"),
  saplings  = file.path(data_dir, "Sapling_MASTER_DBDWith2026.xlsx"))

head(trees)
table(trees$source)
```

Every row is a *tree record*: one tallied tree (or sapling class) carrying
the number of trees per acre it represents. That's the input format for
every growth model in this demo.

> **Check your understanding.** Pick one overstory row and recompute its `tpa`
> by hand. You'll need `attr(trees, "n_plots")` for the number of points in the stand.

# Describe the forest

`stand_summary()` reports the standard stand metrics. Every one of them is
also a standalone function in the package (`qmd()`, `stand.density.index()`,
`relative.density.index()`, …).

```{r summary}
stands <- stand_summary(trees)
stands$acres <- as.numeric(attr(trees, "stand_acres")[stands$stand])

stands |>
  arrange(desc(acres)) |>
  select(stand, acres, tpa, ba, qmd, sdi, top_ht, vol_cuft, lead_spp, lead_share) |>
  head(10) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 1)))
```

```{r forest-composition, fig.height = 4}
trees |>
  mutate(ba = 0.005454154 * dbh^2 * tpa,
         acres = as.numeric(attr(trees, "stand_acres")[stand])) |>
  group_by(fvs) |>
  summarise(ba = sum(ba * acres) / sum(stands$acres)) |>
  slice_max(ba, n = 10) |>
  ggplot(aes(ba, reorder(fvs, ba))) +
  geom_col(fill = pal[1], width = 0.7) +
  labs(x = "Forest-wide basal area (ft²/ac)", y = NULL,
       title = "Demeritt Forest is a white pine – hemlock – red maple forest")
```

```{r stand-scatter}
ggplot(stands, aes(qmd, tpa, size = acres)) +
  geom_point(colour = pal[1], alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_y_log10() + scale_size_area(max_size = 6) +
  labs(x = "Quadratic mean diameter (in.)", y = "Trees per acre (log scale)",
       size = "Stand acres", title = "Stand density vs. size: 153 stands")
```

The scatter above is the raw material for a stand density management diagram.
A good first capstone exercise is to add Reineke lines (SDI = 100, 200, …)
with `stand.density.index()` and see where Demeritt stands sit.

# Growth engine 1: the CONUS model (runs anywhere)

`conus_project()` implements the **FVS Remodeling Project** equations
(Johnson, Marshall & Weiskittel; github.com/holoros/fvs_remodeling). That
project is refitting FVS components across the lower 48 states with a single
set of species-level equations, one variant for everything. Each year, every
tree record gets:

| component | depends on |
|---|---|
| diameter growth | DBH, crown length, basal area in larger trees (BAL), elevation, extreme min. temperature |
| height growth | height, crown ratio, crown competition in larger trees, crown closure at the tip, climate |
| survival | crown ratio, crown closure at the tip |
| crown recession | height growth, crown closure |

The climate covariates (`elev` in ft; `emt` and `td` in °C from ClimateNA
1991–2020 normals) default to rough values for Orono. Replacing them with
real ClimateNA values is an early task.

Start with one stand:

```{r one-stand}
one <- filter(trees, stand == "A116")
stand_summary(one)

res <- conus_project(one, years = 50)
res$summary |> select(year, tpa, ba, qmd, sdi, top_ht, vol_cuft) |> round(1)
```

Notice basal area *drops* over the first five years. A116 starts at an SDI of
531, above 85% of its species-weighted maximum, so the density backstop
(Section 8) thins it by mortality before growth catches up. Compiled FVS
does much the same thing (Section 7).

Under the hood these are ordinary R functions you can call yourself. Here's
next year's diameter growth for each tree in A116:

```{r components}
cmp <- conus_competition(one$dbh, one$ht, one$cr, one$tpa, one$fvs)
one |>
  mutate(bal = cmp$bal,
         dg  = conus_dg(spcd, dbh, cr, ht, cmp$bal, elev = 150, emt = -32)) |>
  select(fvs, dbh, ht, cr, tpa, bal, dg) |>
  arrange(desc(dbh)) |> head(8) |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))
```

# Silviculture: comparing regimes

Treatments are defined once with `treatment()` and work in both engines. As in
FVS, the residual-basal-area target counts only trees eligible for cutting.

```{r regimes}
regimes <- list(
  "No action"          = list(),
  "Thin to 90 now"     = list(treatment(0,  "thin_below", residual_ba = 90, min_dbh = 4.5)),
  "Thin to 90, twice"  = list(treatment(0,  "thin_below", residual_ba = 90, min_dbh = 4.5),
                              treatment(25, "thin_below", residual_ba = 90, min_dbh = 4.5)),
  "Clearcut at 25"     = list(treatment(25, "clearcut")))

case <- filter(trees, stand %in% c("A116", "K151", "R204"))

runs <- bind_rows(lapply(names(regimes), function(r)
  project_stands(case, "conus", years = 50, regime = regimes[[r]]) |>
    mutate(regime = r)))
```

```{r regime-plot, fig.height = 5}
runs |>
  mutate(regime = factor(regime, names(regimes))) |>
  ggplot(aes(year, ba, colour = regime)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ stand) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal) +
  labs(x = "Years from 2025", y = "Basal area (ft²/ac)", colour = NULL,
       title = "Basal area under four regimes (CONUS engine)",
       subtitle = "Rows show the stand before each year's treatment")
```

Standing plus harvested volume is the yield you compare across regimes:

```{r regime-table}
runs |>
  group_by(stand, regime) |>
  summarise(harvested_cuft = sum(removed_vol),
            standing_cuft_yr50 = vol_cuft[year == 50],
            total_cuft = harvested_cuft + standing_cuft_yr50, .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), round)) |>
  arrange(stand, desc(total_cuft))
```

> No regeneration model runs inside the CONUS engine. After a clearcut the
> stand stays empty unless you add a regeneration tree list yourself. A
> clearcut regime is therefore only useful for counting the harvest itself.

# The whole forest

Projecting all 153 stands takes about 15 seconds:

```{r forest}
forest <- project_stands(trees, "conus", years = 50)

acres <- attr(trees, "stand_acres")
forest_total <- forest |>
  mutate(acres = as.numeric(acres[stand])) |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarise(vol_mcf = sum(vol_cuft * acres) / 1000,
            ba = weighted.mean(ba, acres))

ggplot(forest_total, aes(year, vol_mcf)) +
  geom_line(colour = pal[1], linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(colour = pal[1], size = 2) +
  labs(x = "Years from 2025", y = "Standing volume (thousand ft³)",
       title = "Demeritt Forest standing volume, no harvest (CONUS engine)")
```

# Growth engine 2: compiled FVS (Northeast variant)

`fvs_project()` writes each stand's tree list and one keyword file, runs the
FVS executable, and reads FVS's own summary table back from its output
database. The returned columns match the CONUS engine's, so the two can be
compared directly. The run folder is kept so you can open `run.key` and
`run.out` and see exactly what FVS did. That's the best way to learn FVS
keywords.

```{r fvs-available}
fvs_ok <- !is.na(fvs_find("ne"))
fvs_ok
```

```{r fvs-run, eval = fvs_ok}
fvs <- project_stands(trees, "fvs", years = 50, cycle = 5)

both <- bind_rows(forest, fvs) |>
  mutate(acres = as.numeric(acres[stand])) |>
  group_by(engine, year) |>
  summarise(across(c(ba, tpa, qmd, top_ht, vol_cuft), ~ weighted.mean(.x, acres)),
            .groups = "drop")

both |>
  pivot_longer(c(ba, tpa, top_ht, vol_cuft)) |>
  mutate(name = recode(name, ba = "Basal area (ft²/ac)", tpa = "Trees per acre",
                       top_ht = "Top height (ft)", vol_cuft = "Total volume (ft³/ac)")) |>
  ggplot(aes(year, value, colour = engine)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ name, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal) +
  labs(x = "Years from 2025", y = NULL, colour = NULL,
       title = "Same tree lists, two growth engines (area-weighted forest means)")
```

```{r fvs-skip, eval = !fvs_ok, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
cat("*FVS was not found on this machine, so this comparison was skipped.",
    "Install FVS and set `options(MEForLab.fvs_dir = ...)` to run it.*")
```

Both engines start from identical tree lists and heights
(`pass_ht = "all"`). Any divergence therefore comes from the growth, mortality
and regeneration models, not from the starting data. Figuring out *why* they
diverge is a capstone project in itself.

# Sensitivity: what drives the projection?

Every model input is an assumption. Here are three to probe with the CONUS
engine.

```{r sensitivity, fig.height = 4.5}
sens <- list(
  "Default"                    = list(),
  "Colder site (EMT -36 °C)"   = list(site = list(elev = 150, emt = -36, td = 29.5)),
  "No density backstop"        = list(sdi_limit = NA),
  "Diameter growth +20%"       = list(mult = list(dg = 1.2)))

sens_runs <- bind_rows(lapply(names(sens), function(s)
  do.call(project_stands, c(list(trees = case, engine = "conus", years = 50), sens[[s]])) |>
    mutate(run = s)))

sens_runs |>
  mutate(run = factor(run, names(sens))) |>
  ggplot(aes(year, ba, colour = run)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ stand) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal) +
  labs(x = "Years from 2025", y = "Basal area (ft²/ac)", colour = NULL)
```

`sdi_limit` needs a note. The CONUS survival equation only knows crown ratio
and crown closure *above* a tree. A sapling record carrying 500 identical
stems/ac has no taller neighbours, so it barely dies and the stand grows past
any biologically possible density. The backstop caps stand SDI at 85% of the
species-weighted FVS-NE maximum. It is an addition to the remodeling-project
equations, so say so whenever you report results that use it.

# Known limitations

* **Heights are imputed, not measured.** Every height comes from the Wykoff
  equation. Measuring a subsample of heights next season would let you
  calibrate it.
* **Climate inputs are placeholders.** Pull ClimateNA 1991–2020 normals for
  Demeritt's coordinates (`DBD_2025_INV_Points.zip`).
* **The CONUS equations are preliminary.** They're still being refit, and
  crown closure at the tip (CCH) is approximated here because the project's
  crown-profile code isn't published yet.
* **The CONUS engine has no regeneration or ingrowth.** FVS-NE adds stump
  sprouts after cutting.
* **Volumes come from Honer-form equations (`vol.calc()`) in the CONUS engine
  and from NVEL in FVS.** Compare growth in basal area before you compare
  volume.

# Possible capstone questions

1. **Which engine is right for Demeritt?** Use remeasured plots (CFI or FIA in
   Penobscot County) to test both engines' 5–10-year predictions.
2. **Thinning regimes for white pine–hemlock.** Which residual BA and entry
   interval maximizes sawtimber volume over 50 years?
3. **Climate sensitivity.** How much do projected yields change under a
   warmer climate (ClimateNA future normals for `emt` and `td`)?
4. **Height imputation.** How much do projections change when heights come
   from a different height–diameter model? Compare `wykoff.ht()` against
   FVS-imputed heights (`pass_ht = "measured"`).
